source_interpretation.topic: An excess nitrogen-source feed is distinct from reaction stoichiometry
source_interpretation.text: The net reaction shown by the authors consumes Al and NH4Cl in a 1:1 ratio, whereas their best experimental charge ratio is NH4Cl:Al = 3:1. Lower-ratio diffraction patterns retain unreacted Al. The authors associate at least 3:1 with more complete reaction; this is an empirical feed condition, not a revised stoichiometric equation.

evidence.locator: Main PDF p. 1–2, Equation 1; Figure 4 and feed-ratio discussion

source_interpretation.text: The authors propose NH4Cl decomposition followed by chloridization of Al and reaction of volatile aluminum chlorides with NH3. The cited 339 °C decomposition value, subchloride equilibrium and gas–gas growth picture are contextual hypotheses. No transient aluminum-chloride species, gas composition or mechanism is directly measured. All seven source equations remain accessible in the source context.

evidence.locator: Main PDF p. 1–2, Equations 1–7 and mechanism discussion

source_interpretation.text: The paper proposes that increasing NH4Cl raises autoclave pressure and benefits crystallization, but reports no measured pressure. At about 500 °C the AlN has very poor crystallinity; the selected method uses 580 °C. Increasing temperature is described as growing particles and improving crystallinity, without a numerical size-versus-temperature series.

evidence.locator: Main PDF p. 2, Feed-ratio and processing-temperature discussions

source_interpretation.topic: Different size measurements answer different questions
source_interpretation.text: The 6 nm Scherrer estimate describes diffraction coherence; the rounded 6 nm TEM mean and the 5.85 nm histogram-derived mean describe particle projections. The histogram spans 3–11 nm and reports a standard deviation of 0.57 without an explicit unit. These observations are kept distinct instead of being averaged into one invented measurement.

evidence.locator: Main PDF p. 1–2, Figures 1–3 and size discussion

source_interpretation.text: Small oxide reflections are attributed as a possibility to surface oxidation of the commercial Al powder. The source distinguishes oxide impurity from the residual Al associated with incomplete reaction at lower NH4Cl feeds. Neither impurity fraction nor precursor oxide coverage is quantified.

evidence.locator: Main PDF p. 1–2, Figures 1 and 4 impurity assignments
